facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: Built in the thirteenth century, it was conceived as a gigantic solar chariot with twelve pairs of exquisitely-ornamented wheels dragged by seven rearing horses.
facts.text: The temple base was engineered as a colossal solar chariot featuring 24 elaborately sculpted stone wheels drawn by seven horses.

facts.label: legend
facts.quote: There is a lodestone at the top of the temple was said to be a massive 52 ton magnet. According to legend, the statue of the Sun God inside the temple was built of a material with iron content and was said to be floating in air.
facts.text: Local folklore claims a massive 52-tonne lodestone magnet sat atop the main temple tower to suspend an iron-bearing idol in mid-air.

facts.label: legend
facts.quote: Due to its magnetic effects, vessels passing through the Konark sea were drawn to it, resulting in heavy damage. Other legends state that magnetic effects of the lodestone disturbed ships' compasses so that they did not function correctly.
facts.text: Maritime lore states that the magnetic force of the temple spire pulled passing sea vessels toward the coast and caused compasses to malfunction.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: To save their shipping, the Portuguese voyagers took away the lodestone... But there is no record of this occurrence in any historical records, nor is there any record of the existence of such a powerful lodestone at Konark Temple.
facts.source_name: Archaeological Survey of India & Scientific Literature
facts.text: While folklore asserts Portuguese navigators removed the crowning magnet to save their ships and caused the temple to crumble, historians and the ASI document no historical record of a lodestone and attribute structural failure to unstable sand subsoil and weathering.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: Until fairly recent times, in fact, the temple was close enough to the shore to be used as a navigational point by European sailors, who referred to it as the 'Black Pagoda'.
facts.text: While popular stories claim European sailors called Konark the Black Pagoda because of magnetic shipwrecks, maritime navigational records show sailors used its dark silhouette against coastal sand solely as a visual navigational landmark.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: Some of the iron beams of Konarka (now 32 in number) are massive, around 30 ft. in length and weigh around 8 tons.
facts.text: Archaeological documentation by the Archaeological Survey of India has recorded 32 massive wrought-iron beams integrated horizontally into the stone masonry as lintel supports.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: The Konark iron beams demonstrated corrosion resistance almost two orders higher than contemporary steel beams, even though the iron beams may lack certain properties like ductility and weldability.
facts.source_name: Archaeological Survey of India & IIT Bhubaneswar
facts.text: In 2023 CE, metallurgical testing conducted with the Archaeological Survey of India revealed that the medieval Konark iron beams have corrosion resistance two orders of magnitude higher than modern structural steel.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: The KT's wheel functions as a vertical sundial, meticulously designed to align with the exact latitude of Konark... allowing for the accurate determination of time throughout the day, with minimal error, by casting shadows.
facts.source_name: Archaeological Survey of India & Scientific Literature
facts.text: Field studies confirm that the wheels of the Konark Sun Temple are engineered as vertical sundials with 8 major spokes that demarcate the eight three-hour prahars of the day.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: The sundial has 8 major spokes that devide 24 hours in to 8 equal parts... Again there are 30 beads in between one major and one minor spoke, so one bead is equivalent to 3 mins.
facts.text: The functional sundial wheels feature 30 carved beads along the rim segments between spokes, which allow time observation in three-minute divisions.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: Samba, a son of Krishna was cursed to be afflicted by leprosy... In chapter 14, Samba engaged himself in tapas, meditating on Surya at Mitravan... subsequently being cured by worshipping Surya in the temple constructed by him.
facts.text: The Samba Purana records that Samba, son of Krishna, underwent 12 years of penance dedicated to Surya on the riverbanks to find relief from leprosy.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: The Madala Panji of Puri Jagannath temple describes how Kalapahad attacked Orissa in 1568... he somehow managed to displace the Dadhinauti (Arch stone) and thus weaken the temple leading to its collapse.
facts.text: The Madala Panji chronicle of the Jagannath Temple records that general Kalapahad struck the Konark complex in 1568 CE and dislodged its crowning arch stone.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: The Jagamohan was filled with sand by the British between 1901 and 1903 to prevent structural collapse and provide stability to the monument.
facts.text: In 1903 CE, British colonial conservators filled the assembly hall interior with sand and walled up the doors to halt structural settlement.
